references.text: Describes how Esau sold his birthright for a meal, providing context for his intense hunger and desire to eat the red stew that Jacob prepared.
Explicitly identifies Esau as Edom, confirming the origin of the name from the incident with the red stew in Genesis 25:30.
Refers to Esau as Edom in the mountains of Seir, linking back to why he was called Edom based on the incident with the red stew.
Warns against immorality and godlessness by using Esau as an example, who sold his birthright for a single meal.
27:36 confirms the consequence of the action described in 25:30; the birthright lost for food.
Thematic parallel: Jacob's use of food/gifts in meeting with Esau, first as payment for rights, later as atonement.
